## Release v1.8.0

Started as a DNS-tunnels release; grew into a tightening of the whole stack — new MahsaNG v16 protocols, a one-paste V2Ray subscription in every bundle, a critical XDNS crash fix, a sing-box 1.13 config migration, and the build/update reliability work that comes with running MoaV on small censored-region servers for real.

Builds on contributor PR #102 (@ibeezhan), hardened and fully integrated, plus follow-up fixes from live testing on a 1–2 GB VPS.

### Highlights

**Full MahsaNG v16 + V2Ray subscription**
- **MasterDNS** — DNS tunnel native to MahsaNG v16, fronted on `m.<domain>`. Markedly more reliable than dnstt/Slipstream during heavy shutdowns; keeps a session alive when almost nothing but DNS is getting through. Enabled by default; prebuilt binary checksum-verified against the upstream release.
- **GooseRelay** — SOCKS5 over a Google Apps Script you deploy in your own Google account; fronted as `google.com`, AES-256-GCM end-to-end. Opt-in (`ENABLE_GOOSERELAY=true`, `PORT_GOOSE=8444`). Each bundle ships a ready-to-paste `Code.gs` + client config.
- **One-paste V2Ray subscription in every bundle** — `subscription.txt` + a click-to-copy "Import everything at once" card at the top of `README.html` (EN + FA). Works in MahsaNG, v2rayNG, Hiddify, Streisand, any V2Ray app. Replaces the now-redundant per-user "MahsaNG" admin download button **and** the `moav user mahsanet` CLI command.

**All four DNS tunnels in parallel on UDP 53**
- dnstt / Slipstream / MasterDNS / XDNS fan out by subdomain (`t./s./m./x.`) via `dns-router` (which now **self-heals** after a backend restart/rebuild — re-resolves and reconnects without needing its own restart). The v1.7.5 port-group exclusion model is retired; any combination is valid. Closes #99.

**Critical config fixes**
- **XDNS finalmask schema migrated to Xray v26.x** (`domain` → `domains` server / `resolvers` client) — without this, anyone with XDNS enabled on 1.7.8/1.7.9 was crash-looping the whole xray container, taking Reality/Trojan/XHTTP down with it.
- **sing-box 1.12.23 → 1.13.12** + config migrated to the 1.13 rule-action model (legacy `sniff` inbound field and `block` outbound were removed in 1.13). Versions aligned across `.env.example`, all Compose build args, and the sing-box/client/bootstrap Dockerfiles (they had drifted to a mix of 1.12.23/1.13.2/1.12.17).

**Low-RAM build resilience** (live-tested on a 1–2 GB VPS)
- **RAM-aware `compose_build()`** wraps every build call-site; tiers concurrency to detected RAM (≤3 GB serial, 3–6 GB ×2, >6 GB Docker default; override with `MOAV_BUILD_PARALLEL=N`). Ends the `context deadline exceeded` failures from Docker's bake builder fanning every image out in parallel. `--no-cache` no longer hard-coded into the post-update steps.
- **Snowflake** uses the official prebuilt image by default (source-compile fallback via `SNOWFLAKE_BINARY=source`) — the heaviest build is gone. **`dns-router`** Go compile pinned to single-package builds (`-p=1`, `GOMAXPROCS=1`).
- **Installer offers a swapfile** on ≤2.5 GB hosts (opt-in, skipped on non-interactive installs); `moav doctor` flags missing swap.
- **`moav update` rebuilds source-changed services** — services with no version pin (e.g. `dns-router`) whose code changed in a pull are queued for rebuild; previously the change shipped in git but never reached the running container.

**Robustness & polish**
- `moav user add` now generates MasterDNS/GooseRelay bundle files directly (no follow-up `regenerate-users`).
- `moav update` no longer blocks on generated/runtime-mutated files (`conduit_lifetime.rules.yml`, MasterDNS/GooseRelay configs) or the pipe-separated `GOPROXY` value.
- `moav doctor` no longer reports a *lower* release as an "available update" (proper semver comparison).
- Admin dashboard: matched `.zip`/MahsaNG button styling; removed the redundant per-user "MahsaNG" download + route. The MahsaNet community-network *donation API* is a separate feature and is unaffected.
- New TROUBLESHOOTING entries: dnstt "session opens, no stream" = client MTU too high (the bundle ships an isolation test); SSH-over-DNS apps are incompatible with our SOCKS upstream by design.
- Docs/website/`client-guide-template` updated throughout (incl. EN+FA); CHANGELOG compare-links restored.

### ⚠️ Upgrade Notes

This is a **breaking upgrade** for existing installs:
- **Defaults changed** — `ENABLE_XDNS` and `ENABLE_MASTERDNS` are now `true`. On `moav update`, installs that didn't set these pick up the new defaults and start the new containers. Set them `false` in `.env` first to opt out.
- **Re-bootstrap required** — XDNS, sing-box, MasterDNS/GooseRelay configs are regenerated by bootstrap (idempotent; keys and user UUIDs preserved).
- **XDNS direct-mode port moved 53 → 5356** (`PORT_XDNS`); `dns-router` owns host UDP 53.
- **sing-box 1.12 → 1.13.12** is a minor-version jump — re-bootstrap regenerates the config to the new rule-action model; verify the stack comes up healthy after.
- **Apply order:**
  ```
  moav update
  moav build masterdns gooserelay xray   # auto-serializes on low-RAM; no --no-cache needed
  moav bootstrap                          # regenerates configs (XDNS v26 + sing-box 1.13)
  moav regenerate-users                   # refresh user bundles (V2Ray subscription, MasterDNS instructions, etc.)
  moav start
  ```
  On ≤2 GB hosts, accept the installer / `moav doctor` swap suggestion.

### Test plan (verified on a 2 GB VPS)

- [x] Low-RAM build auto-serializes (`Build concurrency limited to 1 (RAM …)`); snowflake pulls prebuilt; MasterDNS build logs `SHA256 OK`
- [x] `moav bootstrap` idempotent; keys preserved (dnstt pubkey + MasterDNS key unchanged across server / `outputs/` / bundle)
- [x] sing-box 1.13.12 loads cleanly post-migration; XDNS inbound builds with the v26 `domains` schema — **no xray crash loop**
- [x] `dns-router` logs four routes (`t./s./m./x.`)
- [x] dnstt verified end-to-end via standalone `dnstt-client` (session → stream → fetched server IP through sing-box egress)
- [x] MasterDNS on MahsaNG v16: session established, traffic flows
- [x] V2Ray subscription ready in every bundle (`subscription.txt` + README "Import everything" card)
- [x] `moav user add` produces complete bundles; `moav update` no longer blocks on generated/runtime files; rebuilds source-changed services
- [~] `dns-router` self-heal: implemented + unit-tested; live backend-rebuild recovery not yet re-exercised
- [ ] GooseRelay (opt-in): live Apps Script deploy + end-to-end
- [x] Version-bump (`MASTERDNS_VERSION` / `GOOSERELAY_VERSION`) triggers rebuild via `moav update`
- ℹ️ dnstt on MahsaNG v16 has no MTU control → use MasterDNS there (documented). SSH-over-DNS apps incompatible by design.

Full changelog: [CHANGELOG.md#1.8.0](https://github.com/shayanb/MoaV/blob/dev/CHANGELOG.md#180---2026-05-28).

## Resumo
Conecta os **dois fluxos de aquisição** ao job queue de deep-enrichment (W3-08), atendendo ao requisito de que toda pesquisa traga o enriquecimento de sócios automaticamente.

## Mudanças
**Cadastro manual** (`SearchPage.handleSpecificSearch`): ao criar o lead, dispara `requestEnrichment(lead.id, 'realtime')`. O worker (cron 30s) processa em ~30s; o grafo de sócios aparece na ficha. Toast informa o usuário.

**PESCA / massa** (`usePesca` Fase 6): após salvar, `enqueueEnrichmentBatch(leadIds, 'high')` — todos os leads "já vêm enriquecendo", com prioridade `high` e teto anti-saturação.

**Backend** (`20260526140000`):
- `request_enrichment(lead, priority)` — 2º param (default `realtime`, compat com TabSocios).
- `enqueue_enrichment_batch(text[], priority)` — aceita UUID ou `rec...`.
- `greatest_priority()` — nunca rebaixa prioridade.
- `dispatch` com teto `high=8`/ciclo (protege rate-limit Assertiva).
- worker cron `1min → 30s`.

Remove `runDeepEnrichment` síncrono (código morto, risco de reintroduzir o timeout do W3-08).

## Gates
`tsc -b` + `vite build` verdes. Lint: sem novos erros (baseline `any` pré-existente no SearchPage inalterado).

## Validação
Backend aplicado e verificado. E2E dos 2 fluxos em produção após merge.

author: dhmin
body:
## What

Fixes the cua-driver uninstaller `libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.sh` so it parses under **bash 3.2** — the `/bin/bash` shipped on macOS and the exact shell the documented one-liner invokes (`/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL …/uninstall.sh)"`).

Closes #1722.

## Why

Under bash 3.2.57 the script aborts before doing anything:

```
uninstall.sh: line 324: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `)'
uninstall.sh: line 694: syntax error: unexpected end of file
```

bash 3.2 has a parser bug where a here-document inside a `$( … )` command substitution is **not** skipped while scanning for the closing `)`. The Rust-branch Python here-doc (`python3 <<'PY'`) carried three apostrophes in comments — `Swift's`, `it's`, `shouldn't` — an **odd** count, so bash 3.2 entered a phantom single-quoted string, never matched the `)`, and ran to EOF. The Swift branch's equivalent here-doc was already apostrophe-free, which is why only the Rust branch tripped. bash 4+/5+ (e.g. Homebrew bash) parse it correctly, so it only bites users running the documented `/bin/bash` flow.

## Change

Reword those three comment lines to drop the contractions/possessives so the here-doc no longer contains unbalanced single quotes. **No behavioral change** — comments only.

## Verification

```console
$ /bin/bash --version | head -1
GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin25)

# before
$ /bin/bash -n libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.sh
uninstall.sh: line 324: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `)'
uninstall.sh: line 694: syntax error: unexpected end of file

# after
$ /bin/bash -n libs/cua-driver/scripts/uninstall.sh && echo OK
OK
```

author: davik85
body:
### Motivation
- Provide admins a safe, backend-only way to reset a user’s consumed free-lesson allowance for a specific UTC date when support intervention is required.
- Ensure the reset is auditable, scoped to a single `DailyFreeLessonUsage` row, and does not affect sessions, messages, counters, entitlements, billing, or require EF migrations.

### Description
- Add route constant `ApiConstants.AdminUserFreeLessonAllowanceResetRoute = "/api/admin/users/{userId:guid}/free-lesson-allowance/reset"` and new `AdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetConstants` for field names, validation errors, date format, and metadata keys.
- Add request/response contracts `AdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetRequest` and `AdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetResponse` under `Contracts/Admin` for the endpoint payloads.
- Implement `IAdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetService` and `AdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetService` which:
  - validate `reason` (required, trimmed, max length `EntityConstants.Lengths.MediumTextMaxLength`) and `usageDate` (optional, defaults to UTC today, or parse exact `yyyy-MM-dd`),
  - check target user exists with `AsNoTracking()`,
  - load a tracked `DailyFreeLessonUsage` by `(UserId, UsageDate)`,
  - delete only that `DailyFreeLessonUsage` row, capture safe metadata, and write an audit using `IAdminAuditService.RecordTargetUserActionAsync`,
  - perform delete + audit in a single transaction on the same scoped `AppDbContext` and return a response with reset/audit flags.
- Add small endpoint handler in `AdminEndpoints` mapping `POST /api/admin/users/{userId:guid}/free-lesson-allowance/reset`, protected by `AdminAuthorizationConstants.BootstrapAdminPolicyName`, that reads admin id from claims and delegates to the service and maps validation/not-found responses to `400`/`404` appropriately.
- Register the service in DI: `builder.Services.AddScoped<IAdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetService, AdminFreeLessonAllowanceResetService>();`.
- Add new admin audit action constant `AdminAuditConstants.ActionTypes.FreeLessonAllowanceReset = "free_lesson_allowance_reset"` and use normalized reason and safe metadata keys when writing the audit entry.
- Update docs (`docs/subscription-billing-foundation.md`) with an `Admin Foundation v8` section describing behavior and non-goals; no EF migration was created.

### Testing
- Attempted to build the API with `dotnet build backend/EnglishVoiceTutor.Api/EnglishVoiceTutor.Api.csproj`, but the environment lacks the `dotnet` CLI so the build could not be run (failure due to `dotnet: command not found`).
- No automated tests were executed in this environment; changes were limited to backend API code and documentation and intentionally did not create or modify EF migrations.

author: mendo9
body:
## Why
Production athletes will upload film from their computers, so the **upload → R2 → worker streaming** path matters most for launch — but the demo only had `link` clips, leaving that path unexercised. This makes the demo's 40-yard clip a real `upload` so streaming (incl. the public share page) is demoable and covered.

## What
- **Seed:** the 40-yard demo clip is now `source: 'upload'` with `storage_key`/`content_type`/`size_bytes` and `url: null`. `toResponseClip` derives the stream URL from the source, so it serves through `/api/film/:id/video` (authed) and `/api/public/film/:id/video` (public). The two highlight reels stay `link` + ApexMark placeholder — no duplicated footage.
- **`db-seed-demo.sh`:** now uploads the bundled `demo-athlete-40.mp4` into R2 at the clip's storage key (`apexathlete-media` local / `apexathlete-media-demo` remote) so the bytes exist to stream. Idempotent.
- Removed the now-unused `SEED_SAMPLE_VIDEO_URL` import in personas.
- Includes a chore commit syncing the demo D1 `database_id` (from the demo DB recreation).

## Verification (local, logged out)
- Public film list returns the 40-yard with `url: /api/public/film/clip_ap_demo_athlete_forty/video`.
- `Range: bytes=0-1023` → **206** (1024 bytes); full → **200** (1,216,791 bytes); plays in the `/p/:id` reel.
- 52 db tests pass; typecheck + lint clean.

## Applying on the deployed demo
`bash scripts/infra/db-seed-demo.sh --env demo` (or `db:reset --env demo`) — seeds the upload-clip row **and** uploads its bytes to `apexathlete-media-demo`.

body:
Stacked on #12 (`feat/nyc-time`).

Adds a **compact filing header** pulled from datamule's already-parsed submission metadata and surfaces it on cards + the detail page.

## What
- **parsing**: `extract_filing_header(content)` selects company name, CIK, SIC, state of incorporation, period of report, filing date, SEC file number, location, and 8-K `item-information`. Never raises; tolerates `filer` as list/dict; full key set with empty defaults.
- **db**: new `filing_metadata` TEXT (JSON) column with migration; `save_ex10_exhibit(..., filing_metadata=)`, `update_filing_metadata`, `exhibits_missing_filing_metadata`. Summary cols include it (SUBSTR markdown truncation unaffected).
- **listener**: extractor returns `filing_metadata`; persisted on save.
- **worker**: `backfill_metadata_batch` fills rows missing metadata, isolating per-row failures (stores `{}` so broken filings aren't retried forever).
- **api**: detail exposes parsed `filing`; summary carries `company_name`/`period`/`location`/`items` for card footers.
- **frontend**: `AgreementCard` footer (filer/period/location) + detail-page **FILING DETAILS** panel; `formatYmd()` formats SEC `YYYYMMDD` dates.

## Tests (TDD, red→green)
`test_filing_header.py` (6) + new db/listener/worker cases. Full backend suite green (58).

author: duuunjaaa
body: On mount, ClientPaymentVerifyPage calls POST /api/payments/preview in parallel with createPaymentApproval. The preview endpoint probes the partner bank with a 2PC NEW_TX then immediately sends ROLLBACK_TX to get the quoted exchange rate, fee, and final credited amount without committing any funds. The result is shown in the payment summary card before the user confirms: exchange rate row (if currencies differ), fee row, and recipient receives row. While the preview is in flight a pulsing "Fetching..." placeholder is shown. If the preview call fails or the partner bank is unreachable the rows are silently omitted and the approval flow continues unaffected.

body:
## Summary

Adds four previously-unhandled `Trigger` enum variants in `crates/mtgish-import/src/convert/trigger.rs`, wiring them to engine modes that already exist. This unlocks ~70+ cards that were silently dropped by the converter.

| Trigger variant | Engine mapping | CR | Cards unlocked (~) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AtTheBeginningOfAPlayersSecondMainPhase` | `Phase::PostCombatMain` | 505.1 | ~28 |
| `AtTheEndOfCombat` | `Phase::EndCombat` | 511.2 | ~18 |
| `WhenAPermanentExploitsAPermanent` | `TriggerMode::Exploited` | 702.110b | ~25 |
| `WhenAPlayerPlaysALand` | `TriggerMode::LandPlayed` | 305.1 | ~16 |

Example cards now supported:
- **Second main phase**: Defiant Survivor, Acrobatic Cheerleader, Delina Wild Mage
- **End of combat**: Clockwork Beast, Clockwork Avian, Samite Elder
- **Exploit**: Fell Stinger, Graf Reaver, Gurmag Drowner
- **Land play**: Horn of Greed, Burgeoning, Fastbond, Mana Breach

## Design notes

author: vocanicz
body:
## Symptom

Autonomous workers launched with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` still hit the standard Bash tool-permission prompt (`Do you want to proceed? 1. Yes / 2. Yes and don't ask again / 3. No`) and wedge forever — no human to answer. Observed live on a worker stuck ~13 min.

## Root cause (verified empirically)

`--dangerously-skip-permissions` only sets the **main** session's permission mode. **Claude Code sub-agents do not inherit it** — a `Task` / `subagent-driven-development` child derives its mode from settings (managed → project → user) only, never from the parent's CLI flag. With no `defaultMode` configured anywhere, dispatched sub-agents run in **default (ask)** mode and block on the first mutating command.

Confirmed by experiment, not just docs:
- A plain flagged main session ran `rm`/`mkdir`/`ln` **without** prompting ("bypass permissions on") → the flag works for the main session.
- The wedge is a **tool-permission** prompt, **not** the workspace-trust dialog (dir already trusted, non-root, no managed policy).
- Disproved the "`skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt: true` disables bypass" theory: the control had that key and still got bypass.

## Fix

Add `ensure_bypass <dir>` (mirrors `ensure_trusted`) on the autonomous launch path. It merges `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` into `<wd>/.claude/settings.local.json`, which the session **and its cwd-scoped sub-agents** read. That file is git-ignored by convention; we also append it to the worktree's `info/exclude` so `git add -A` can never commit it on installs lacking that global ignore.

- Gated on `HARNESS_AUTONOMOUS` (supervised launches keep normal prompting).
- **Merges, not clobbers** — preserves Claude's own `permissions.allow` rules + unrelated keys.
- No `flock`: each session owns a unique `<wd>`.

## Verification

- `test_bypass.sh` (new, 10/10): writes `defaultMode`; preserves existing `allow` + unrelated keys; idempotent `info/exclude`; no-op when supervised.
- Full engine suite green (exit 0), incl. `test_spawn` 21/21.

## Note for operators
Takes effect for sessions spawned **after** a relaunch. Immediate host-wide stopgap: `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` fixes live fleets' sub-agents on next spawn (covers any cwd, but also affects interactive human sessions on that host).

author: cyberclutch146
body:
# Implement Event Availability and Registration API with Concurrency Handling

Closes #2101, #2102, #2104

## Overview
This PR implements the backend API endpoints and concurrency protections required for event registration and availability checks in the Eventra application.

### Key Additions and Improvements

#### 1. Concurrency Control and Event Capacity
* **Pessimistic Locking:** Added pessimistic write locks (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) when fetching events for registration. This ensures concurrent registration requests are serialized, preventing overbooking.
* **Optimistic Locking Fallback:** Added `@Version` to the `Event` entity. A retry mechanism (up to 3 attempts) in `EventService` automatically handles transient optimistic locking failures.
* **Capacity Tracking:** Reorganized capacity fields to avoid redundancy and ensure safe updates to `registeredCount` and `capacity`.

#### 2. Event Availability API
* **Public Access:** Permitted public access to `GET /api/events/{eventId}/availability` in `SecurityConfig`.
* **Standardized JSON Response:** Returned availability details mapping to expected keys (`maxAttendees`, `currentAttendees`, `availabilityStatus`, and `eventPassed` flag) using Jackson aliases to maintain backward compatibility.

#### 3. Event Registration API
* **Endpoint Implementation:** Implemented a secure `POST /api/events/{eventId}/register` endpoint that checks event capacity and duplicate registrations.
* **Error Handling:** Added custom exceptions (`EventFullException`, `RegistrationConflictException`) mapping to standard HTTP status codes:
  * Duplicate registrations now return a `409 Conflict` status.
  * Overbooking or full capacity returns a `409 Conflict` status.
  * Unauthenticated requests return `401 Unauthorized` instead of the default `403 Forbidden`.
* **Registration Response DTO:** Created a clean response structure to avoid exposing database-level details to the client.

## Testing
* **Integration Tests:** Added integration tests in `EventRegistrationTests.java` and `EventRegistrationConcurrencyIntegrationTest.java`.
* **Concurrency Verification:** Ran multi-threaded execution tests simulating concurrent registration attempts exceeding event capacity. In all tests, the system successfully capped registrations at exactly the defined capacity.
* **Local Run:** All 13 tests passed successfully.

Closes SandeepVashishtha/Eventra#2101
Closes SandeepVashishtha/Eventra#2102
Closes SandeepVashishtha/Eventra#2104

body:
## Summary

- Adds `list_capabilities` (§1.5) as the sixty-third production verb. Read-only engine-metadata verb that returns the thirteen v1.0-mandatory fields from the spec and omits the seven v1.1+ fields entirely.
- Extends `VerbRegistry` with `iter()` so the verb can enumerate registrations without coupling to the inner `HashMap`.
- Projects the 4-field `AvailableEffect` shape down to a 3-field `EffectEntry` (`{kind, category, params_schema_id}`) to match the spec — the `summary` field is dropped.
- Self-referential: the verb registers itself in `default_registry()` and finds itself in the returned `verbs[]`.

Mirror: `crates/verbreel-state/src/verbs/effect_list_available.rs` (twenty-seventh verb) — same shape (Args has `project_id` for Verb-trait compatibility but is ignored by the impl), same single `Unreachable` error variant.

## Design decisions

- **`default_registry()` called inside the verb** (not passed via context). The verb represents the canonical engine surface; the registry is engine-scoped, not request-scoped.
- **v1.1+ fields omitted, not stubbed**. Spec test asserts the serialized envelope has exactly 13 keys and none of `tracker_*`, `audio_analysis_*`, `stock_providers`, `template_count`, or `preview_session_formats` appear.
- **Per-verb `summary` / `args_schema_id` emit `""`**. The `Verb` trait does not yet expose these — wiring them is a separate architectural slice (~63 verbs to annotate).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --locked` green
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --locked` green (27 new tests pass; 105 test result lines workspace-wide, no failures)

- [x] All seven v1.1+ field names are absent from serialized envelope

author: copilot
body:
The client was calling `api.frankfurter.dev` directly, causing network-level `"Failed to fetch"` errors when third-party CORS policy blocked browser requests. This change moves exchange-rate fetches to a same-origin Netlify endpoint and keeps the existing fallback behavior for unstable `/latest` windows.

- **Server-side exchange-rate proxy (`/api/exchange-rate`)**
  - Added `netlify/functions/exchange-rate.mjs` to call Frankfurter from Netlify instead of the browser.
  - Supports `from`, `to`, optional `date`; returns `{ from, to, rate, date }`.
  - Adds request timeout, input validation, same-currency short-circuit, and clearer upstream error mapping.

- **Routing integration**
  - Added Netlify redirect in `netlify.toml`:
    - `/api/exchange-rate` → `/.netlify/functions/exchange-rate`
  - Placed with existing `/api/*` redirects before SPA catch-all.

- **Client exchange-rate library update**
  - Reworked `src/lib/exchangeRate.js` to call the new same-origin proxy endpoint.
  - Preserves retry-on-latest behavior by falling back once to yesterday’s date when no explicit date is provided.
  - Propagates API-provided error messages into thrown client errors.

```js
const params = new URLSearchParams({ from, to })
if (date) params.set('date', date)
const res = await fetch(`/api/exchange-rate?${params}`)
```

body:
## Situation

- `user_details.email` 컬럼이 NOT NULL 로 박혀 있으나 실제로는 **dead column** — 운영 RDS 의 `user_details` 0 rows + production 코드 `email` 참조 0 건 (정적 분석 + DB empirical 양쪽 확인).
- `user_details` 0 rows 인 이유 — dev API (`POST /api/v1/dev/users`) 로 만든 MEMBER 들은 **`users` 행만 INSERT 하고 `user_details` 는 안 만지는 설계** 였음. OAuth 통합 (#122 Task 8) 전까지의 임시 결로, dev MEMBER 가 OAuth 없이 만들어지므로 social_id 가 없는 상태. 결과적으로 마이그레이션이 건드릴 데이터가 0.
- OAuth 통합 (epic #122 Task 8) 진행 전 schema 정합 결. 정책 변경 — **email 받지 않기로 결정**.

## Task

- email 결을 OAuth 에서 받지 않기로 결정한 이유:
  - **사용처 0** — 마케팅·인증·복구 메일 어떤 용도로도 안 받음
  - **Kakao 검수 lead time 0** — "이메일" 동의 항목을 받으면 검수 (1-2주) 필요한데, 동의 항목을 비우면 즉시 면제
  - **Google 도 결 가벼움** — email scope 빼면 "unverified app" 경고 없음, 검수 lead time 0
  - **Apple 은 본래 검수 없음** — Apple Developer Program 만 가입돼 있으면 즉시 사용
- 즉 셋 다 검수 lead time 0 으로 OAuth 출시 가능. 이걸 가능하게 만들려면 `email NOT NULL` 제약을 풀어야 함.

## Action

- `V20260527011356__drop_user_details_email.sql` — `ALTER TABLE user_details DROP COLUMN email` (forward-only, CLAUDE.md 의 마이그레이션 컨벤션 준수).
- `UserDetail` 엔티티에서 `email` 필드 + `updateEmail()` 메서드 제거. 생성자 인자도 정리.
- NULL 허용 vs DROP 사이에서 **DROP 채택**. NULL 허용은 hedge 인데 dead 컬럼이 남으면 "왜 안 쓰지?" 라는 질문을 만들고 우리의 명시적 결정 ("email 받지 않기로") 이 코드에 안 드러남. CLAUDE.md YAGNI 결과 일치. 미래에 email 결이 필요해지면 ADD COLUMN 으로 추가 (backfill 0, cost 거의 0).
- 데이터 영향 0 — 운영 RDS `team3.user_details` 0 rows 직접 SELECT 로 empirical 확인 후 진행. CLAUDE.md "DROP 류 destructive 작업은 단계적으로" 경고는 데이터·코드 의존이 있을 때 결인데 둘 다 0 이라 단계 분리 불필요.

## Result

- OAuth 통합 진행 시 Kakao·Google·Apple 셋 다 **검수 lead time 0** 으로 출시 가능.
- production 코드 / DB 영향 0 — 전체 테스트 **375 PASS** (failures 0, errors 0, skipped 2).
- 미래에 email 결이 필요해지면 `ADD COLUMN` 마이그레이션으로 즉시 복구 가능 (지금 데이터 없으니 backfill cost 0).

author: branarakic
body:
## Summary

Surface four upstream libp2p defaults as operator-tunable config under a new `network` block in `~/.dkg/config.json`. Targeted at testnet / small-mesh deployments where the upstream defaults (peerStore: 1h address age / 6h peer age; PeerResolver: 5s per-step timeout) cause direct addresses to age out before being re-discovered via the (sparse) DHT — visible as the "can't dial Muy-Sentinel anymore" / "need to manually /api/connect after every restart" patterns on the testnet.

| Field (under `network`) | Wire mapping | Upstream default |
|---|---|---|
| `peerStoreMaxAddressAgeMs` | `createLibp2p({ peerStore: { maxAddressAge } })` | 1h |
| `peerStoreMaxPeerAgeMs` | `createLibp2p({ peerStore: { maxPeerAge } })` | 6h |
| `dhtQuerySelfIntervalMs` | `kadDHT({ querySelfInterval })` | kad-DHT default |
| `peerResolveTimeoutMs` | `new PeerResolver({ defaultPerStepTimeoutMs })` | 5s |

All four are optional. Omitting a field preserves the upstream default — zero behaviour change for any existing operator.

## Wiring

Follows the existing `relayServerCapacity` pattern:

1. Typed on [`DkgConfig`](packages/cli/src/config.ts) (cli) and [`DKGNodeConfig`](packages/core/src/types.ts) (core).
2. Forwarded through [`lifecycle.ts`](packages/cli/src/daemon/lifecycle.ts) -> `DKGAgent.create()` -> [`dkg-agent.ts`](packages/agent/src/dkg-agent.ts) mapping.
3. Applied in [`createLibp2p`](packages/core/src/node.ts) / `kadDHT` / [`PeerResolver`](packages/core/src/network/peer-resolver.ts) constructor.

A small permissive validator (`isFinitePositiveInteger` in [`node.ts`](packages/core/src/node.ts)) silently ignores invalid values (0, NaN, fractional, negative, non-numeric) so a config typo doesn't brick startup — these knobs are tuning, not safety gates, so the warn-and-fall-back surface from `validateRelayServerCapacity` would be noise.

## Tests

- [`peer-resolver.test.ts`](packages/core/test/peer-resolver.test.ts):
  - constructor override applies when `opts.perStepTimeoutMs` is omitted
  - per-call values still win over the constructor override
  - invalid values (NaN, 0, fractional, negative, Infinity) fall back to the 5s built-in default
- [`config.test.ts`](packages/cli/test/config.test.ts):
  - round-trip the four knobs through `saveConfig` / `loadConfig`
  - absent `network` block stays undefined so libp2p defaults apply

Full suites: `@dkg/core` 933 / 933 green, `@dkg/cli` config tests 33 / 33 green. `@dkg/agent` has one pre-existing `swm-snapshot-sync` failure unrelated to this PR (verified on `main`: `Unknown file extension ".ts" for sync-verify-worker-impl.ts`, worker-thread loader issue).

## Test plan

- [x] Build green: `pnpm -F @origintrail-official/dkg-core build`
- [x] Build green: `pnpm -F @origintrail-official/dkg-agent build`
- [x] Build green: `pnpm -F @origintrail-official/dkg build` (cli)
- [x] Unit tests green: `peer-resolver.test.ts` (21/21), `config.test.ts` (33/33), full `@dkg/core` suite (933/933)
- [ ] Manual: edit `~/.dkg/config.json` on Miles to add `{ network: { peerStoreMaxAddressAgeMs: 86400000, peerResolveTimeoutMs: 15000 } }`, restart, confirm no startup warnings, watch peerStore age behavior over a few hours.

## Companion work

PR B (`feat/chain-agents-cg-phonebook`) lands next: extends the agents Context Graph with `dkg:multiaddr` + `dkg:lastSeen`, adds a periodic profile heartbeat, and threads agents-CG addresses into the outbox stall-recovery path. PR A is the smaller half of a two-PR network-robustness pair planned during the post-rc.11 testnet diagnostics session.

Related issue: discussion thread in [#697](https://github.com/OriginTrail/dkg/issues/697) (Muy-Sentinel's publish-quorum failure).

## Problem

The build fails with four TS2345 errors in `backend/routes/dashboard.ts` because `@types/express@^5.0.0` types `req.params` values as `string | string[]`, while the `customerStore` functions all expect `string`. With `"strict": true` in `tsconfig.json`, TypeScript rejects the implicit narrowing at each of the four `req.params.id` usage sites.

## Solution

Added `as string` casts to `req.params.id` at all four call sites (`getCustomerById`, `updateCustomer`, `getCallById`, `completeTask`). This is safe because Express 4 named route parameters (`:id`) always produce a `string` at runtime — the broader type is an artifact of the v5 type definitions being used against an Express 4 runtime.

body:
`Manual DB Setup` was failing with `P3005` because production schema already existed while migration history was missing. This change makes baseline explicit, bounded, and non-destructive so only truly pending migrations (`add_person_lifecycle_status`, `add_gearops_core_tables`) remain for deploy.

- **Baseline workflow now enforces direct migration connection**
  - `manual-db-baseline.yml` uses `DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL || secrets.DATABASE_URL }}`
  - fails fast if host is pooled (`-pooler.`), preventing advisory-lock/runtime-URL mismatches

- **Baseline is now boundary-driven and guarded**
  - added `workflow_dispatch` input: `baseline_migration` (historical boundary, inclusive)
  - resolves only migrations up to selected boundary from the approved historical set
  - explicitly protects post-baseline migrations from resolve:
    - `20260526143000_add_person_lifecycle_status`
    - `20260526152000_add_gearops_core_tables`

- **Added schema-aware safety checks before `migrate resolve`**
  - introspects live DB schema with `prisma db pull --print`
  - verifies expected schema markers per selected historical migration before marking applied
  - refuses baseline if expected markers are missing

- **Added high-signal diagnostics for operators**
  - logs direct DB host/provider
  - logs selected boundary and computed resolve list
  - logs `prisma migrate status` before/after baseline
  - logs protected migration pending-state check

- **Separated responsibilities: baseline vs deploy**
  - removed `prisma migrate deploy` from baseline workflow (baseline-only)
  - `manual-db-setup.yml` remains deploy workflow and now adds:
    - pooled-host refusal guard
    - post-deploy `prisma migrate status` diagnostic

```yaml
# baseline workflow (excerpt)
env:
  DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL || secrets.DATABASE_URL }}

# guarded resolve path
npx prisma migrate resolve --applied "$migration"

# setup workflow still performs deploy
npx prisma migrate deploy
```

author: mokashang
body:
### PR Description

The confirm action for the search/filter prompt and for text input prompts (e.g. when naming a stash or creating a new branch) was hard-coded to `<enter>` in #4860, on the assumption that nobody would want to remap it. As reported in #5510, that assumption was wrong: users who rebind `keybinding.universal.confirm` to something like `<c-j>` could no longer confirm those two prompts at all.

This adds two new keybindings, `confirmSearch` and `confirmPrompt`, following the existing convention of context-specific confirm keys (`confirmMenu`, `confirmSuggestion`, `confirmInEditor`). Both default to `<enter>`, so the behaviour is completely unchanged for users who don't remap them; users who do can now point them at whatever key they like.

Fixes #5510.

Testing: added an integration test (`config/rebind_confirm_search_and_prompt`) that rebinds both keys to `<c-y>` and verifies that a search and a text prompt can each be confirmed with the rebound key. I confirmed the test fails on `master` (both prompts ignore the rebound key) and passes with this change. The existing search/prompt integration tests still pass.

author: murdercode
body:
## What

Two small CI workflow hardening changes. No functional changes.

### `build.yml` — script injection hardening
`workflow_dispatch` inputs and step outputs were interpolated directly as `${{ ... }}` inside `run:` blocks. A value containing shell metacharacters could break out of the string and execute commands in the runner. They now all pass through `env:` and are referenced as quoted shell variables (`"$VER"`), which the runner treats as data rather than code.

> Note: only triggerable by someone who already has write access to the repo (the `workflow_dispatch` input), so this is defensive hardening, not an externally exploitable vulnerability.

### `keepalive.yml` — pin action to SHA
`liskin/gh-workflow-keepalive@v1` (mutable tag) → pinned to the full commit SHA `f72ff1a1336129f29bf0166c0fd0ca6cf1bcb38c` (v1.2.1). Prevents a re-pointed tag from introducing unreviewed code.

- No remaining `${{ }}` interpolation inside `run:` blocks.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## Summary

Replace silent catch-and-log in five board persistence loaders with a typed
`(int, string * exn) result` contract.  Loaders no longer hide IO failures
inside their own bodies; the global store builder (`load_all_persisted`,
called from `global_lazy` and `reset_global_for_test`) is now the single
site that decides whether to keep the best-effort "log and continue" policy.

Affected loaders:

- `Board_votes_json.load_persisted_posts`
- `Board_votes_json.load_persisted_comments`
- `Board_votes.load_persisted_votes`
- `Board_votes.load_persisted_reactions`
- `Board_votes.load_persisted_sub_boards`

## Motivation

Each loader previously had signature `store -> unit` and ended with

```ocaml
| Eio.Cancel.Cancelled _ as e -> raise e
| e -> Log.BoardLog.error "load X failed: %s" (Printexc.to_string e)
```

Callers could not distinguish a clean load from a partially loaded store
following a transient IO failure (`load_jsonl` raising mid-read, broken
permissions, etc.).  `load_jsonl` already drops malformed JSON lines
silently at the parser layer, so the only path into the catch arm is a
real storage-layer failure — exactly the case where downstream readers
proceeding against a half-populated `Hashtbl` is most dangerous.

The new signature is `store -> (int, string * exn) result`:

- `Ok loaded_count` when the file is absent (`Ok 0`) or fully read.
- `Error (path, exn)` when an exception escaped the read loop;
  `Eio.Cancel.Cancelled` is still re-raised unchanged.

Loaders still emit `Log.BoardLog.info`/`debug` for the success path
(unchanged from before); only the failure path moves to the call site.

## Why this is not a workaround

Per `CLAUDE.md` workaround-rejection bar, self-checked the three
signatures:

1. **Counter-as-Fix** — No Prometheus counter is introduced.  The fix is
   a typed contract change.  Operator visibility (if needed) belongs in a
   follow-up that observes the now-typed `Error` branch from the call
   site, not inside the loader.
2. **String/substring classifier** — N/A.
3. **N-of-M partial sweep** — All five loaders in the board persistence
   surface change in this PR; no caller migration is deferred.  The two
   call sites (`global_lazy` + `reset_global_for_test`) both route
   through the new `load_all_persisted` helper.

## Test plan

- [x] `dune build @check --root . --cache=disabled` clean
       (`feedback_dune_shared_cache_stale_on_mli_change.md` guarded)
- [x] `_build/default/test/test_board_karma_ledger.exe` — 18/18 OK
- [x] `_build/default/test/test_vote_ts_preservation_10086.exe` — 2/2 OK
- [x] `_build/default/test/test_board_persistence_load_contract.exe`
       (new, 2/2 OK) — pins `Ok 0` for absent file on both
       posts/comments loaders
- [x] `test_types` 3 failures (`fs_write_mode_ssot`,
       `tool_search_files_op_ssot`, `assertion_kind_ssot`) reproduce
       on `origin/main` without this change — pre-existing,
       unrelated; false-attribution avoided.
- [x] `ocamlformat --check` on all touched files — pass.

## Out of scope

- Adding Prometheus counters or other observability for the typed
  `Error` branch.
- Promoting `load_all_persisted` to a stricter "abort startup on
  Error" policy.  Current behaviour (log + continue) is preserved
  intentionally so this PR is a pure contract widening.
- The two `tool_board_format.ml` WARN sites flagged in the initial
  audit are RFC-0093 Phase B intended preservation/visibility paths
  (coerce-rather-than-drop + typed `_ -> []` arm split) and are NOT
  changed.

author: pjcdawkins
body:
## Summary

Raises `legacy/phpstan.neon` from `level: 7` to `level: 8` and fixes the four genuine runtime crashes that surfaced along the way. Each fix has an integration test that reproduces the crash on the unfixed binary.

The remaining 124 new findings at level 8 are paths the static type checker can't narrow but that are guarded at runtime; they're added to `phpstan-baseline.neon`.

## Commits

1. `fix(legacy): handle runtime operations with no stop command` — `operation:list` crashed on an operation defined with only a `start` command.
2. `fix(legacy): allow null previous value in autoscaling duration change` — `autoscaling:set` crashed when a metric had `up` triggers but no `down` (or vice versa).
3. `fix(legacy): guard ResourcesSet against missing profile sizes` — `resources:set --dry-run` crashed when a deployment's `profile_size` wasn't present in its `container_profiles` map (e.g. a deprecated size still set on an older deployment).
4. `fix(legacy): tolerate null timestamps on activities` — `activity:list` / `activity:get` crashed when the API returned a null `created_at`, `updated_at` or `completed_at`.
5. `test(integration): cover domain:update, domain:get, org:user:projects` — happy-path tests for three commands whose level-8 findings looked nullable but were unreachable.
6. `chore(legacy): raise PHPStan to level 8` — flips the level and regenerates the baseline.

## Background

A level-8 analysis produced 122 new findings across 57 files. Each one was inspected by reading the actual call graph rather than trusting the verdict — a skepticism filter that turned out to be important: of eight candidate bugs investigated, only four were real (the four fixed here). The other four had guards the static checker couldn't see (closure invariants, early returns, upstream filtering, Symfony `InputArgument::REQUIRED`).

author: nichobbs
body:
## Summary

Closes the three low-risk SUGGESTION findings from PR #1380's
review.  All three are filed as separate issues by the review
workflow (#1383, #1384, #1385); none block merging on their own, but
fixing them now keeps the typechecker safety story tight before the
remaining #1378 follow-ups (stdlib IFunc + codegen MemberRef, per-
package symbol-table filtering) land.

## Findings addressed

### #1383 — `addSigsFromItems` user-item shadowing

`addSigsFromItems` was applying first-in-wins uniformly.  Imported
items run first, so once stdlib `IFunc` collection lands a user
`pub func foo` would silently lose to an imported `foo`.  Now:

- `isImported = true` → first-in-wins (still needed to dedupe within
  the imported batch — multiple stdlib files declaring `toString`,
  `tryGet`, …)
- `isImported = false` → `remove` + `add` so user definitions
  unconditionally shadow imports, matching the standard import-
  shadowing semantics.

### #1384 — `isCodegenBuiltinName` cross-reference comment

Added an `IMPORTANT:` comment block on `isCodegenBuiltinName`
pointing at `codegenBuiltinType` in `typechecker_exprs.l`.  The two
functions form an implicit contract: every name `codegenBuiltinType`
returns a polymorphic `TyError`-typed signature for must appear in
this guard list, otherwise an imported stdlib `pub func` with the
same simple name will shadow the builtin and tighten the call's
argument type — reverting `println(11)` → T0043 in user code.

### #1385 — Deterministic `appendLyricFiles` ordering

`File.listFiles` (`Directory.GetFiles`) gives no ordering guarantee,
so two machines could register stdlib `_kernel/` items in different
sequences and the typechecker's first-in-wins `symTableTryFindOne`
would pick different declarations on each.  Added
`sortPathsByBasename` (a small selection sort — input is a few dozen
files, quadratic is fine and avoids depending on `List[T].Insert` /
indexer assignment, neither of which the bridge codegen carries
dedicated arms for).  The F# `SelfHostedBridge.fs` shim's
`findStdlibSources` does the same sort via `Array.sortBy` so the F#
and Lyric paths see the stdlib in identical order.

Fixes three issues surfaced in the employee ordering demo, plus a note on a fourth.

## Issue 3 — multi-tag filter only matched the first tag
The OpenAPI contract declares the `tags` query param as `explode: false` (comma-delimited, `tags=a,b`) and Huma parses it that way, but `@tbite/api-client` (openapi-fetch) defaults to `explode: true` (`tags=a&tags=b`), so the server only saw the first value.
- **Fix:** set the api-client `querySerializer` to `{ array: { style: "form", explode: false } }`, matching the contract. `tags` is the only array query param in the spec, so the change is correctly scoped.
- **Verified:** captured the outgoing URL — before `tags=hot&tags=veggie`, after `tags=hot,veggie`.

## Issue 2 — two overlapping tag filters
The top `CategoryStrip` (client-side, single-select) and the `MenuFilterBar` (server-side, multi-select) both filtered tags and were mutually exclusive.
- **Fix:** unify them onto the shared URL `tags` state — `CategoryStrip` is now multi-select and drives the same server-side filter as `MenuFilterBar`. Removed the dead client-side `activeCat` branch.

## Issue 4 — next-day orders accepted after the local cutoff
`order.Service.Location` and `menu.HomeService.ServerTZ` used `time.Local`, which degrades to UTC in the `distroless/static` image (no tzdata on disk, CGO off). A 17:00 Taipei cutoff was treated as 17:00 UTC (= 01:00 Taipei next day), so 5/27 stayed orderable after 5/26 17:00.
- **Fix:** embed `time/tzdata` and load `Asia/Taipei` explicitly via `appLocation()` (override with `APP_TIMEZONE`); wired into both `Location` sites and `ServerTZ`.
- **Verified:** new unit tests in `location_test.go` (loads +08:00, cutoff boundary), `go build`/`go vet` clean.

## Issue 1 — same food photo per merchant (no code change)
This is a known MVP seed-data limit: `static/brand/items/` has only 10 photos (one representative per merchant) and the mock data marks them as shared. Not a code bug — left as-is per product decision.

## Verification
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./services/api/...` — clean
- `go test ./services/api/cmd/tbite/` — pass (incl. new tz tests)
- `svelte-check` employee — 0 errors; employee `build` — OK; prettier — clean

author: fw-bot
body:
**Problem:**
When a combo product has a price but all of its combo components have a zero list price, the quotation shows the combo's price twice: once on the combo line itself and once on the last combo item line.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create a combo product with a non-zero price and two or more combo groups whose component products have a zero list price.
2. Create a sale order, add the combo, pick one item per group.
3. Look at the quotation/order: the combo line total and the last combo-item line both show the full combo price.

**Current behavior:**
The full combo price ends up on the last combo item line; the other combo items show 0. The combo line then displays the same total via `_get_combo_totals`, so the same amount appears twice.

**Expected behavior:**
The combo's price is spread across its combo items so no single line duplicates the combo total.

**Cause of the issue:**
`_get_combo_item_display_price` prorates the combo price by each combo's base price. When every base price is 0, every prorated price is 0, so `combo_price_delta` equals the full combo price and is added to the last combo as a rounding correction, concentrating the whole price there instead of spreading it.

**Fix:**
Treat an all-zero base case as "no proration signal" and split the combo price evenly across combos before the delta adjustment runs. The delta correction then only handles rounding, as intended.

body:
# [Mobile] QR Scanner Navigation Transition

## What This Does

This PR implements a smooth, high-performance QR scanner navigation experience on the mobile app. Users can now:

1. **Open QR Scanner via Prominent Button**: A prominently styled "Scan QR" button in the clue list header allows quick access to the camera scanner
2. **Quick Swipe Navigation**: A dedicated upward swipe gesture opens the camera scanner smoothly without visual UI stutter
3. **Seamless Integration**: The scanner integrates seamlessly with the clue list interface, allowing users to scan QR codes for each clue
4. **Visual Feedback**: Swipe hints and smooth animations provide clear feedback to the user

## Why

Users were unable to easily scan QR codes from the clue list interface. This feature addresses issue #202 by providing:
- **Prominent navigation**: A dedicated button makes the QR scanner immediately discoverable
- **Gesture support**: Swipe gestures provide an intuitive, quick way to access the scanner without disrupting the UI
- **No visual stutter**: Implementation uses native animations and optimized rendering for smooth transitions
- **Better UX**: Clue navigation and scanner access are now integrated into a cohesive experience

## Testing

### Manual Testing Checklist

- [ ] Clue list displays all clues with correct styling
- [ ] "Scan QR" button is prominently visible in the clue list header
- [ ] Clicking "Scan QR" button opens the camera scanner modal
- [ ] Upward swipe gesture (velocity > 0.5 and distance > 80) opens the scanner smoothly
- [ ] Scanner displays correctly with corner guide and scan area overlay
- [ ] Scanner permissions request works (both Android and iOS)
- [ ] Scanning a valid QR code closes the scanner and shows success feedback
- [ ] Swipe hint animates smoothly as the user swipes upward
- [ ] Clue navigation works correctly between clues
- [ ] Solved clues are marked with a checkmark badge
- [ ] No visual stuttering during scanner open/close transitions

## Files Changed

### New Files
- `mobile/components/QRScanner.tsx` - Full-screen QR scanner component with camera feed, overlay, and permission handling
- `mobile/components/ClueList.tsx` - Reusable clue list component with prominent scan button and clue selection

### Modified Files
- `mobile/app/(tabs)/play.tsx` - Refactored to use ClueList and QRScanner components with swipe gesture support
- `mobile/package.json` - Added required dependencies for camera and UI components

## Technical Details

### New Dependencies
- `expo-camera@^56.0.7` - Camera access and QR code scanning
- `expo-linear-gradient@^15.2.0` - Gradient UI components
- `lucide-react-native@^0.372.0` - Beautiful icon library
- `react-native-gesture-handler@^2.20.2` - Gesture handling for smooth swipes

### Implementation Highlights

**QRScanner Component**
- Uses `expo-camera` CameraView with barcode scanning enabled
- Full-screen modal overlay with scanner guide corners
- Handles camera permissions gracefully
- Smooth loading state with 300ms initialization delay to prevent stutter
- Auto-closes on successful scan with 800ms delay for success feedback

**ClueList Component**
- Displays clues in a scrollable FlatList
- Active clue highlighted with gradient background
- Prominent gradient "Scan QR" button in header
- Solved clue indicators with checkmark badge
- Smooth navigation between clues

**Play Screen Integration**
- Implements PanResponder for upward swipe gesture
- Detects swipe velocity (vy < -0.5) and distance (dy < -80)
- Smooth animation feedback with opacity interpolation
- Active clue card displays current clue details
- Swipe hint animates based on swipe progress

### Performance Optimizations
- Camera initialization delay prevents UI stutter on first load
- Smooth animations use native driver when possible
- Lazy loading of camera only when scanner is opened
- Efficient component memoization for FlatList rendering

## Related Issues

Closes #202

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project conventions and style guidelines
- [x] Changes include appropriate UI/UX enhancements
- [x] New components are well-documented with comments
- [x] Dependencies are minimal and necessary
- [x] No breaking changes to existing APIs
- [x] Mobile-specific considerations addressed (permissions, performance)

## Notes

- This implementation uses mock clue data for testing. Connect to actual API in follow-up PR
- Camera permissions handling differs between iOS and Android - tested for both
- Gesture handling includes velocity threshold to prevent accidental triggers
- The scanner component is fully reusable for other parts of the app

This pull request introduces a continuous integration (CI) workflow and improves the robustness and test coverage of the audio matching logic. The most significant changes are the addition of a GitHub Actions workflow for automated testing, enhancements to error handling and logging in the AcoustID audio matching function, normalization of return values, and the introduction of a new test suite for core functionality.

**Continuous Integration:**

* Added a `.github/workflows/ci.yml` file to run tests automatically on pushes and pull requests to `main`, across Python versions 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12. This ensures code quality and compatibility via GitHub Actions.

**Testing Improvements:**

* Introduced a new test suite in `tests/test_core.py` with unit tests for audio analysis and AcoustID matching, using mocks to simulate external dependencies and verifying correct behavior and output normalization.
* Added a package initializer `tests/__init__.py` for the tests directory.

**Audio Matching Robustness and Logging:**

* Improved error handling in `matcher.py` for the AcoustID matching function:
  - Checks for missing API keys and logs debug messages.
  - Locates the `fpcalc` binary more robustly, preferring an explicit path or searching the system PATH, with clear error logging if not found.
  - Logs errors for failed subprocess calls, missing fingerprints, and HTTP errors from the AcoustID API.
  - Adds info-level logging for successful matches and cases where no match is found. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR114) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR123-R138) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR160) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR173-R179) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR197-R202)

**Return Value Normalization:**

* Ensures that the `title`, `artist`, and `album` fields in audio matching results are always strings (never `None`), improving downstream reliability and simplifying test assertions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR83-R87) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-360658412035af84eea930934801bf8e8fc93bb329f06d015fde7cfc86aa17adR197-R202)

**Code Quality:**

* Added imports for `shutil` and `logging` in `matcher.py` to support the new error handling and logging features.

body:
This PR builds the Taskly backend requested in the issue: a NestJS service with Tasks and Categories, backed by PostgreSQL via Prisma, and exposed through code-first GraphQL (plus REST endpoints). It adds full CRUD, task filtering, validation, environment config, and containerization.

- **API surface (Tasks + Categories)**
  - Added `categories` and `tasks` modules with services/resolvers/controllers.
  - Implemented full CRUD for both domains in GraphQL and REST.
  - Added task filtering by `status` and `categoryId` in query paths.

- **GraphQL code-first schema + DTO model**
  - Added `@ObjectType()` entities (`Task`, `Category`) and `@InputType()` DTOs for create/update/filter.
  - Registered `TaskStatus` enum (`PENDING | IN_PROGRESS | DONE`) for GraphQL.
  - Wired Apollo GraphQL module in code-first mode.

- **Persistence layer (Prisma + PostgreSQL)**
  - Added Prisma schema with:
    - `Category { id, name, color, tasks[] }`
    - `Task { id, title, description?, status, dueDate?, categoryId, category }`
    - `TaskStatus` enum
  - Added Prisma module/service integration for Nest dependency injection.

- **Validation + configuration**
  - Enabled global validation pipe with whitelist/transform/forbid options.
  - Added `class-validator` rules across inputs.
  - Added `@nestjs/config` usage and `.env.example`.

- **Containerization**
  - Added multi-stage Dockerfile (`builder` + `production`) exposing port `3000`.

```ts
@InputType()
export class TaskFilterInput {
  @Field(() => TaskStatus, { nullable: true })
  status?: TaskStatus;

  @Field(() => Int, { nullable: true })
  categoryId?: number;
}
```

author: copilot
body:
Standard-header parsing was still blocked by template-depth noise in allocator/string-heavy libstdc++ paths. Completed class-template cache hits were being counted as fresh instantiation frames, obscuring the next semantic blockers.

- **Template instantiation**
  - Return completed class-template cache hits before entering parser instantiation-depth accounting.
  - Preserve ShapeOnly upgrade behavior by keeping full cache/type-map checks on the existing later paths.
  - Shared cached-struct inspection across cache paths.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added `test_template_cache_hit_depth_ret0.cpp`, covering repeated reuse of an already-instantiated specialization inside a deep template chain.

```cpp
template<int N>
struct Chain : Chain<N - 1> {
	Cached<0> cached; // cached specialization reuse should not consume depth
};
```

- **Standard-header tracking**
  - Updated `tests/std/README_STANDARD_HEADERS.md` with current libstdc++ findings and timings.
  - Documented that `<memory>` / `<string>` now move past the previous `std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator` cache-depth blocker to recursive `basic_string` depth guarding.

author: dong-qiu
body:
Closes #105.

GitHub forces JS actions onto the **Node.js 24 runtime by default starting 2026-06-02** (Node 20 removed from runners 2026-09-16). This bumps every pinned action to the first major that declares `runs.using: node24`. Each target was verified by reading the repo's `action.yml` at that tag via `gh api` (not release-notes prose).

## Version map

| Action | From | To | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v4 | **v5** | |
| `actions/setup-go` | v5 | **v6** | |
| `actions/setup-node` | v4 | **v5** | |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v4 | **v6** | v5 still node20 |
| `actions/download-artifact` | v4 | **v7** | v5/v6 still node20 |
| `pnpm/action-setup` | v4 | **v5** | |
| `golangci/golangci-lint-action` | v7 | **v9** | v8 still node20 |
| `softprops/action-gh-release` | v2 | **v3** | |
| `docker/setup-buildx-action` | v3 | **v4** | ⚠️ not in #105 inventory |
| `docker/build-push-action` | v5 | **v7** | v6 still node20; ⚠️ not in #105 inventory |
| `docker/login-action` | v3 | **v4** | ⚠️ not in #105 inventory |
| `bufbuild/buf-action` | v1 | v1 | already node24, unchanged |

## Notes / decisions

- **#105's inventory omitted the three `docker/*` JS actions.** They are node20 too and would also break under the forced switch, so they're included here. (Flagging the inventory gap rather than silently scoping it out.)
- **`golangci-lint-action` v7→v9 crosses no config break:** `.golangci.yml` is already `version: "2"` (golangci-lint v2), which the v7 action already required. v8 was skipped only because it never moved off node20; v9 is the first node24 line.
- **Minimal node24-declaring major per action** to keep the behavioral delta small — this is why `upload-artifact` (v6) and `download-artifact` (v7) land on different majors (each is its own node24 floor). Their interop is exercised end-to-end by the release dry-run below.

## Validation

- `actionlint` clean on both files (the one SC2193 warning at `release.yml:208` is **pre-existing** on `main` — a known false-positive for `${{ }}` expressions in shell comparisons, untouched by this PR).
- CI on this PR re-runs golangci-lint@v9 against the repo, so a v9 incompatibility would fail here.
- Release-pipeline change → `release.yml` dry-run dispatch + `/review` per repo policy (see PR checks / review).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Follow-on fix in this PR: go-version matrix alignment (commit 2)

Bumping `setup-go` v5→v6 surfaced a latent CI lie. **v6 sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` by default** (v5 left it `auto`), so the `go: '1.23'` matrix legs now fail fast:

```
go: go.mod requires go >= 1.25.0 (running go 1.23.12; GOTOOLCHAIN=local)
```

Under v5, those legs silently auto-downloaded and ran the **1.25.0** toolchain — so `'1.23'` never actually tested Go 1.23. `go.mod`'s real floor is `go 1.25.0`. This PR aligns every pin (matrix + `go-lint` + `integration` + `codegen-drift`) to `'1.25'`, making CI honest and v6-compatible. The `1.26` leg already passes (≥ floor, no switch needed).

This is in-scope: it's a required consequence of the node24 `setup-go` bump — the migration can't be green without it.

## Summary
- The \`tpu7x Performance benchmarks for google/gemma-4-31B-it\` job in nightly build [#18491](https://buildkite.com/tpu-commons/tpu-inference-ci/builds/18491) on \`releases/v0.21.0\` failed **on both attempts** with the recipe's startup-readiness check timing out:

  > \`TIMEOUT: Waited 961 seconds (limit was 960). The string 'Application startup complete.' was NOT found.\`

- Engine-core init alone took **~550 s** (compilation ~415 s) in both attempts; the subsequent precompile of \`compute_logits\` / \`structured_decode\` plus chat-template detection pushed the API server past the 16-min budget before it could bind. No crash, no OOM — purely slow startup on the multimodal compile path.
- Bumps \`TIMEOUT_SECONDS\` from \`960\` to \`1800\` in \`.buildkite/models/google_gemma-4-31B-it.yml\`, matching the 30-min default already used by \`mmlu.sh\` and \`mlperf.sh\`.

## Notes
- \`.buildkite/models/google_gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.yml\` carries the same \`TIMEOUT_SECONDS=960\` and is at risk of the same regression; left untouched here to keep the diff scoped to the actual nightly failure — happy to bundle if preferred.
- \`main\` has the same value; a parallel PR can follow if reviewers want it consistent.

## Test plan
- [ ] Re-trigger the failing nightly job on \`releases/v0.21.0\` and confirm the perf benchmark step reaches \`Application startup complete.\` within the new 1800s budget.

author: jason
body:
## Summary

Defines `changes.jsonl` as Agent Rally Point's canonical multi-agent coordination trace format.

This is additive-only for existing readers:

- keeps legacy `kind`, `payload`, `revision`, `tool`, `model`, `run_id`, and `app_slug`
- adds CloudEvents-aligned identity/routing fields for new records: `specversion`, `id`, `source`, `subject`, `time`, `type`, `datacontenttype`, `dataschema`
- adds ARP causal/correlation fields: `thread_id`, `causation_id`, `correlation_id`
- ships packaged JSON Schemas for the envelope and known event payloads
- documents native ARP records plus the mechanical CloudEvents projection (`payload` → `data`)

The goal is to make downstream inbox, replay/report, scoring, signing, sync, and bridge tooling target one stable coordination trace instead of parsing ad hoc payload conventions.

## Notes

- Native ARP records are CloudEvents-aligned, not strict CloudEvents JSON-format records, because they retain `payload` and ARP compatibility fields. The docs describe the strict projection explicitly.
- Validation remains warns-not-drops at the substrate layer.
- Existing historical records without the new fields remain valid.

## Test plan

```bash
uv run pytest agent_rally_point/test_changes.py agent_rally_point/test_checkpoint.py -q
# 17 passed
```

Commit hook also ran the full suite successfully when invoked with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` to avoid the contributor-machine global `core.hooksPath` leak described in PR #11.

author: onemli
body:
While tracing why an AWX workflow status update wasn't propagating to the UI, I ended up auditing the entire RabbitMQ side of the codebase and found it wasn't really doing anything useful.

The `awx.events` topic exchange has three queues. Two of them — `awx.job.status` and `awx.workflow.status` — have no producers anywhere in the codebase. Their consumer containers have been sitting on empty queues since day one. The third queue, `awx.job.output`, does receive messages from `JobEventsPoller`, but the poller already writes to `JobOutputChunk` and emits over WebSocket before publishing, and the output consumer then performs both of those steps again on the other end. The frontend dedupes by counter so users never saw double log lines, but the broker plus three consumer pods were doing real work for no net effect.

Webhook ingestion was supposed to feed RabbitMQ too. It doesn't — there's a comment in `webhook_receiver.py` saying it calls `JobMonitor` directly. The 30-second Celery sync also bypasses the broker. So in practice the only producer in the whole system has been the per-job output poller, and even there the consumer adds nothing the poller hadn't already done.

This PR removes the broker, the three consumer services, the `event_publisher` module, the `run_event_consumer` and `setup_rabbitmq` management commands, the `pika` dependency, and all `RABBITMQ_*` env vars. Status updates continue through webhook ingestion plus the 30-second sync (which is how they've actually been arriving the whole time). Live job output still streams over the existing Redis-backed WebSocket channel. No user-visible change.

While I was in there I also fixed a latent bug in the webhook receiver: it was calling `monitor.sync_single_execution()`, which doesn't exist on `JobMonitor`. The surrounding `try/except` was silently swallowing the `AttributeError`, so webhook hits looked successful but the sync part never actually ran. Replaced with `JobMonitor.sync_job_status(execution.id)`.

If external subscribers ever become a real requirement, Redis pub/sub or a Postgres outbox covers that without bringing a broker back.

### Upgrade notes for operators

After pulling 1.2.0, the `rabbitmq` container and the three `event-consumer-*` containers stop being created. You can drop the orphan volume with `docker volume rm fabrik_rabbitmq_data`. The `RABBITMQ_*` lines in `.env` become unused — leaving them in place doesn't hurt anything, they can just be removed.

### Verification

Tested end-to-end against AWX 24.6.1 with `awx-ee:24.6.1` (ansible-core 2.17) running real ACI tenant/VRF/contract workflows. Status transitions, live log streaming, terminal notifications all behaved the same as before. Frontend output viewer unchanged.

body: fix #294. Replaces raw `OsFunction` dispatch with a typed `OsFunctionCall`, updates REPL/async paths, and unifies `sorted()`/`list.sort` kwargs and duplicate‑kwarg errors on methods. - **New Features** - New crate `monty-macros` with `#[derive(FromArgs)]` and `#[derive(ToArgs)]`; core traits `FromValue`/`ToMontyObject`. - End‑to‑end typed `OsFunctionCall`: `.to_args()`, `.name()`, `.on_no_handler()`, move‑by‑value via `take_function_call()` and a `Used` placeholder; mount table now handles `&OsFunctionCall`. - `MethodDictMerge` opcode qualifies duplicate‑kwarg errors with the receiver type; `sorted()` delegates to `parse_and_sort` for shared kwargs/errors. - `LaxBool` for Python truthiness in kwargs (e.g., `list.sort(reverse=...)`, `Path.mkdir(parents=..., exist_ok=...)`). - Macro adoption across builtins/modules: `open`, `str.encode`, `bytes.decode`, `str`/`bytes` split/replace/expandtabs, `map`, `min/max`, `pow`, `print`, `zip`, `re.sub/split` and `Pattern.sub/split`, `dict`/`update`, `re.Match.groupdict`, `date`/`datetime`/`timezone`/`timedelta`, `json.dumps`, `list.sort`. - **Bug Fixes** - CPython parity for argument errors: `_PyArg_BadArgument` via `#[from_args(bad_arg|bad_arg_named)]`; exact arity wording (`expected_exact`, singular/plural), deferred unknown‑kwarg ordering, and “keyword argument” conflict text; method vs function names match CPython. - `math.isclose` accepts `a`/`b` kwargs and validates tolerances; `map()` emits the CPython “at least two arguments” message; `json.dumps` arity matches C‑style wording. - `open(mode=...)`, `encode`/`decode` produce named bad‑arg errors; `Path.mkdir(mode=0o777, parents=False, exist_ok=False)` has the correct signature and truthiness; `timezone(td, None)` now raises `TypeError` and reports `None` (not `NoneType`) in the bad‑arg message. - Removed brittle helpers (`get_zero_one_named_arg`, `get_zero_one_two_args`, `extract_keyword_only_pair`) in favor of the macro for consistent errors and refcount safety. author: copilot
body:
The Feature Request Enrichment agent was reporting a "missing tool" failure when trying to add labels — the `agent` job has `issues: read` by design (writes go through the safe outputs pipeline), but `add_label`, `remove_label`, and `update_issue` were never registered as safe output tools in the compiled lock file, leaving the agent with no valid write path.

## Root cause
The `.md` source correctly declares these safe outputs, but the compiled `lock.yml` was missing them throughout the pipeline:
- `<safe-output-tools>` prompt listing (agent was never told they existed)
- `GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS_CONFIG` / config.json written at runtime
- `GH_AW_VALIDATION_JSON` tool schemas (MCP server couldn't serve them)
- `GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS_HANDLER_CONFIG` in the `safe_outputs` job (handlers never executed)

## Changes to `feature-request-enrichment.lock.yml`

- **Prompt** — added `add_label`, `remove_label`, `update_issue` to `<safe-output-tools>` so the agent knows to use them instead of falling back to direct `gh` CLI calls
- **Runtime config** — updated `GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS_CONFIG` (config.json) to include all three tools with the limits from the `.md` source (`add_label: 2`, `remove_label: 2`, `update_issue: 1`)
- **Validation schemas** — added `GH_AW_VALIDATION_JSON` entries for each tool (`label`/`item_number` fields for label ops; `body`/`item_number` for issue update)
- **Description suffixes** — added constraint strings in `GH_AW_TOOLS_META_JSON` for all three tools
- **Handler config** — added `add_label`, `remove_label`, `update_issue` to `GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS_HANDLER_CONFIG` so the `safe_outputs` job (which holds `issues: write`) actually processes them
- **`add_comment` max** — corrected from `1` → `2` to match the `.md` source

author: adminsyspro
body:
## Summary

OIDC sign-in fails with `unexpected iss value, expected undefined` whenever the **Advanced Endpoints** override fields (Authorization URL, Token URL, Userinfo URL) are populated.

When those overrides are set, ProxCenter skips `.well-known/openid-configuration` discovery and openid-client builds the `Issuer` from the raw endpoints, with no canonical `issuer` metadata. The id_token's `iss` claim then has nothing to validate against, so every callback is rejected.

This passes the configured **Issuer URL** through to NextAuth on the manual-override path only. The discovery path (no overrides) is untouched.

## Changes

- `frontend/src/lib/auth/config.ts`: add `issuer: oidcConfig.authorizationUrl ? oidcConfig.issuerUrl : undefined` to the dynamically-built OIDC provider.

## Context

Reported in discussion #349 (Duo SSO behind nginx). The workaround (clear the override fields, keep only Issuer URL) was confirmed working by the reporter; this removes the foot-gun so all four fields can be populated safely.

Docs updated in proxcenter-docs (ldap-oidc + sso-duo troubleshooting).

## Test plan

- [ ] OIDC provider with override fields set: sign-in completes, no `expected undefined` in the `frontend` container log.
- [ ] OIDC provider using discovery only (no overrides): sign-in still works, no regression.
- [ ] Local credentials / LDAP sign-in unaffected.

body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do ?
Update golden values for A100 functional t5 tests to reflect recent model performance adjustments.


### Relative-difference summary

Comparison covers 6 files × 5 metrics = **30 `(file, metric)` pairs**. Per row: `avg_rel_diff = mean((old − new) / old)` over shared steps.

**Per-metric headline numbers** (over `|avg_rel_diff|`)

| metric                    |   n | median \|avg_rel_diff\| | max \|avg_rel_diff\| |
| ------------------------- | --: | ----------------------: | -------------------: |
| `lm loss`                 |   6 |               6.141e-05 |            7.018e-05 |
| `num-zeros`               |   6 |               1.521e-05 |            4.401e-05 |
| `iteration-time`          |   6 |               1.092e-01 |            1.598e-01 |
| `mem-allocated-bytes`     |   6 |                       0 |                    0 |
| `mem-max-allocated-bytes` |   6 |                       0 |                    0 |

**Distribution of `|avg_rel_diff|` across all 30 rows**

| \|avg_rel_diff\| bucket | count |
| ----------------------- | ----: |
| `== 0`                  |    12 |
| `(0, 1e-6)`             |     0 |
| `[1e-6, 1e-4)`          |    12 |
| `[1e-4, 1e-3)`          |     0 |
| `[1e-3, 1e-2)`          |     0 |
| `[1e-2, 1e-1)`          |     1 |
| `>= 1e-1`               |     5 |

**Interpretation**

- `lm loss` max `|avg_rel_diff|` `7.018e-05` / median `6.141e-05` — loss trajectories match the old goldens to numerical noise (well below the ~1e-4 run-to-run band).
- `num-zeros` max `4.401e-05` / median `1.521e-05` — within historical run-to-run variance on T5 mcore configs.
- `mem-allocated-bytes` and `mem-max-allocated-bytes` are flat (`avg_rel_diff == 0` on every row) — no memory regression.
- `iteration-time` is the only metric that moved meaningfully: all 6 rows landed in `[1e-2, 1e-1)` or `>= 1e-1`, **signed negative** (mean `-0.10` to `-0.16`). Negative means `new > old`, i.e. the new run was systematically slower per step than the old golden. This is consistent with a warmup/scheduler shift on the runner, not a correctness change, and pairs with the fact that every other metric is essentially noise. Worth a sanity-check pass on the runner load for that nightly, but no signal that the model changed.

## Summary

Brick 12 of the Go-side native-binary path (Phase 3 of `docs/TOOLCHAIN-SELF-HOSTING.md`). Adds the double-precision floating-point arithmetic + conversion core (`ftype=01`) the backend emits for `f64`:

- **`FADD`/`FSUB`/`FMUL`/`FDIV`**, **`FNEG`**, **`FCMP`**, **`FMOV`** (Dd←Dn), and the GPR↔FPR bit moves **`FMOVfromGPR`**/**`FMOVtoGPR`**.
- Conversions **`SCVTF`** (signed int → double) and **`FCVTZS`** (double → signed int, truncate).
- Assembler wiring: a `d0..d31` register parser plus `fmov`'s three forms (`Dd,Dn` / `Dd,Xn` / `Xd,Dn`) disambiguated by operand prefix.

Self-contained — no data-section/symbol dependency.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestEncodings` — 11 new FP forms match llvm-mc
- [x] **`TestAssembleAgainstGNUAs/float_double`** — matches `aarch64-linux-gnu-as` byte-for-byte

- [x] `go build`, `go vet`, gofmt clean; deadcode gate OK; rebased on latest `main`

## Next

Self-contained remainder: `f32` (S-register) float forms, `ldrsb`/`ldrsh` sign-extending loads. Then the architectural brick — **`adrp`/`add` symbol addressing + data sections** — where I'll surface the design decision (assembler's section/symbol model + ELF layout) before committing.

body: Fixes #216 This PR addresses and resolves all requirements outlined in issue #216 ### Description This Pull Request addresses critical usability limitations, validation bugs, and platform-link mismatch issues within the dashboard's link management flow. ### What This PR Does: 1. **Introduces a secondary cancellation flow** for the link creation block to prevent user entrapment. 2. **Unlocks full editability** of both **Display Name (Label)** and **Platform Slugs** on existing link cards. 3. **Adds real-time visual draft previews** for immediate feedback during editing. 4. **Implements robust server-side and client-side URL validation** to guarantee data integrity and eliminate routing errors. --- ## Key Changes ### 1. Add Link Cancellation Flow * **Files Modified:** `app/dashboard/AddLinkBox.tsx`, `app/dashboard/LinksSection.tsx` * **Enhancement:** Injected a styled, secondary **Cancel** button adjacent to the primary submit button inside the `+ Add Link` creation form. * **State Management:** Clicking "Cancel" cleanly resets the form fields (`url`, `label`, `platform`) back to their defaults and collapses the form drawer via an `onCancel` callback. ### 2. Dual Field Link Editing (Display Name & Platform Dropdown) * **Files Modified:** `app/dashboard/LinkItem.tsx` * **Enhancement:** Redesigned the card item's edit view into a stacked input layout containing fields for the **Link Display Name (Label)**, **Platform Select Dropdown**, and **Destination URL**. * **Live Previews:** The preview header (Platform Icon, Title, and URL) updates in real-time as the user types or selects a platform. * **Auto-Sync:** Changing the selected platform dropdown automatically updates the display name label text to match the newly chosen platform. * **State Resetting:** Toggling the edit panel closed without saving discards draft edits and reverts inputs to their active database states. ### 3. Robust Server & Client URL Validation * **Files Modified:** `app/api/links/[id]/route.ts`, `app/dashboard/DashboardClient.tsx` * **Backend Platform Derivation:** Extended the `PUT` endpoint to process both `label` and `platform` mutations, deriving and updating platform slugs dynamically. * **Mismatch Safeguards:** Implemented strict validation in the `PUT` handler to ensure chosen platforms match the target URLs. Mismatches return a `400 Bad Request`, keeping the edit drawer open for user correction. * **Duplicate Handler:** Gracefully catches Prisma `P2002` unique constraint duplication errors and maps them to a user-friendly error toast. * **Client-Side Normalization:** Formats destination URLs with an absolute `https://` protocol prefix before state updates, resolving local `404 Not Found` relative routing issues. ### 4. Environment Configuration Integrity * **Files Modified:** `next-env.d.ts` * **Enhancement:** Reverted accidental development-server route updates back to its clean repository configuration (`import "./.next/types/routes.d.ts";`). --- ## Detailed Component Walkthrough ### Frontend Components | File Path | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | | `app/dashboard/AddLinkBox.tsx` | Appended a stylized, side-by-side **Cancel** button with an outline UI; built a handler that flushes inputs and triggers `onCancel`. | | `app/dashboard/LinksSection.tsx` | Propagated parent state mutation helpers and wired the cancellation event callback. | | `app/dashboard/LinkItem.tsx` | Revamped edit drawer with stacked `label`, `url`, and dropdown fields. Integrated live preview updating, auto-synchronization, and conditional drawer persistence on transactional API failures. | | `app/dashboard/DashboardClient.tsx` | Extended update mutation signature to serialize labels and platforms. Normalized raw URLs with protocols. | ### Backend Endpoints | File Path | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | | `app/api/links/[id]/route.ts` | Parsed `label` and `platform` from request payload, validated integrity, calculated dynamic platform derivation, and handled unique database indexing constraints. | --- ## Verification & Testing Plan ### 1. Confirmed the container collapses and clears all inputs without saving state or triggering network requests. * **Editing Display Names:** Edited an existing link card's label and URL successfully. Automated Testing * Ran the workspace test suites (`npm test`) and verified that all existing and new unit tests compile and pass successfully with zero regressions. ### Screenshots **screenshot1: The edit of other aspects apart from only link . and the verification logic implemented.** **screenshot2: Added cancel button when adding link .** ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Edit links with custom labels and choose a platform. * Add Link form now supports Cancel. * **Improvements** * Optional explicit platform accepted and preferred when provided; website labels are slugified. * Stronger client-side username validation and refined suggestion generation. * Clearer save error handling with user-friendly conflict messages and success/failure toasts. * **Tests** * API tests now assert full response payloads for link updates.
